intro: Most people in Belarus speak Russian in daily life, though Belarusian is also an official language and a symbol of national identity.

chapters.title: People and language
text: Minsk, rebuilt after the war in grand Soviet style, is home to about a fifth of the population. Belarusian and Russian are both official. Most people are Orthodox Christians, with a Catholic minority in the west.
The painter Marc Chagall was born near Vitebsk, and writer Svetlana Alexievich won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2015.

chapters.title: Food
text: Draniki, potato pancakes, are the national dish; Belarusians are said to know hundreds of ways to cook potatoes.
